subject: SLA: bespoke retention windows & deletion timeline — HorizonX (Q&A + order form revisions)
messages:
From: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@horizonx.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@horizonx.com
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on bespoke retention windows in order form

Thanks Aditya — quick follow up after our last call. A couple of things we need to clarify before legal will sign the order form: 

1) The order form mentions a 'custom eviction window' up to 180 days for archived conversational contexts. Can you confirm whether that means data is logically deleted at day 180 or if it's queued for manual purge?
2) We need an option for a "safelist" retention for specific PII tokens (customer reference IDs) that should persist for 24 months even if the conversation is otherwise deleted — how would that be represented in the SLA/order form?
3) Are there restoration/restore-hold options after deletion is triggered (e.g., emergency restore within 7 days) and how are those billed?

If you can send a redline or an annotated Order Form that maps each of these items to contract language, that'd help speed sign-off.

—Elaine
Elaine Wu
Senior Head of Compliance, HorizonX
elaine.wu@horizonx.com
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@horizonx.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 10:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on bespoke retention windows in order form

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear list. Answering inline and attaching an annotated order form and retention table. Short answers up front: 

• Custom eviction window (up to 180 days): this is a soft/automated purge policy by default. At day 180 tokens are marked for deletion and queued; deletion is executed automatically within 48 hours of the scheduled purge unless the customer has an active restore-hold. We will add explicit language that the system performs automated deletions unless a written restore request is accepted by Redwood ops.

• Safelist for PII tokens (24 months): we can add a safelist provision as an addendum to the Order Form. The safelist is modeled as a named retention cohort (e.g., "HorizonX PII Cohort") with its own retention clock — the data is excluded from the general eviction queue and retained for the safelist period unless HorizonX requests earlier deletion. We'll add a sample line item and a template for token/field scoping.

• Emergency restore (7-day hold window): we support a 7-day emergency restore hold by default for all deletions; beyond that we can offer a paid restoration service subject to availability. We'll propose billing as a flat fee for post-7-day restores (we have language in the attached order form).

Attached: HorizonX_OrderForm_v1.3.pdf (annotated), Data_Retention_Table.xlsx (example cohorts + timelines).

Next steps: please review the annotated order form. If the safelist scoping looks right, we can push a redline to DocuSign for signature. If legal wants different wording for 'automatic purge' vs 'automatic deletion', call out the preferred term and we'll mirror it.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on bespoke retention windows in order form

Aditya — legal had two short edits to how the safelist is defined and how restores are triggered. Proposed edits below: 

1) Safelist definition: include a clause that safelisted data must have a customer-supplied schema map and be scoped to explicit fields or token patterns; Redwood must provide a confirmation that safelisting will not change model training exposure (we need the assurance).

2) Restore triggers: require that emergency restores be able to be requested via a secure support ticket and that Redwood confirm restore initiation within 4 business hours. If the restore is invoked after the 7-day emergency window, the parties will negotiate a timeline and fees.

Can you ask your legal/ops team to confirm these are acceptable edits? We prefer the wording be included as annotated text in the order form (visible to signers).

—HorizonX Legal (contracts@horizonx.com)
From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: contracts@horizonx.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 15:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on bespoke retention windows in order form

Hi Elaine / Contracts team — I reviewed the suggested edits with engineering/ops. We can accept both bullets with the following clarifications for the Order Form: 

• Safelist schema map: yes, safelisting requires a customer-provided schema map (CSV or JSON). Redwood will ingest the map and apply the safelist rules at the storage layer; we will include a short statement that safelisting does not alter or permit model training on the safelisted fields, and we will provide periodic verification logs (retention cohort manifests) as an appendix in the order form.

• Restore initiation SLA: we confirm a restore initiation acknowledgement within 4 business hours for emergency restores submitted via the secure ticketing endpoint. Implementation note: actual data restoration completion depends on cohort size; the order form will include an estimated restore timeline table (example in attached Data_Retention_Table.xlsx). Restores requested after the 7-day emergency window are handled under our Restoration Services schedule (see section 6 of the attached order form).

If that language works, Aditya — please update the annotated PDF and we can start the DocuSign flow for the HorizonX_OrderForm_v1.3.pdf (final name will be v1.4 after these redlines).

—Dev Patel
Director, Product Ops — Redwood Inference
